scaleflow.text:
Fleet at scale: two levels, one view

1. FLEET (boards 1): one island per orchestrator tree. Hierarchy is drawn only inside an island (orchestrator on top, workers on a tree rail). No edge ever joins two orchestrators. Islands pack into columns: vertical scroll only, never horizontal.
- Sort: needs-you first (CI failed, blocked on the user), then most active.
- Finished workers (done/stopped) fold into one '▸ N done · M stopped' row.
- Remote trees carry a REMOTE · <machine> band with the connection dot (green connected / amber reconnecting / red unreachable); the tree groups orchestrators under their machine; toolbar has a Machine filter.
- The session tree duplicates the islands here, so it starts collapsed to a rail ([ toggles it).

2. ISLAND OPENED (board 2): click an island / Enter on it, or click an orchestrator in the tree. Shows only that orchestrator's tree as full cards with hierarchy edges, sub-orchestrators and ghost plan nodes; finished workers become one stacked card. Breadcrumb Fleet › <orchestrator>; Esc or the breadcrumb returns to 1 with the island still selected. Clicking a worker in the tree opens its orchestrator with that worker selected. Detail panel + bottom action row are context-sensitive to the selection.

This replaces the old shell (sidebar sections, Workers, the 'Fleet overview' section, the TUI Graph tab). It is not an extra section.

Decisions (27 Oct):
- Top nav: Fleet 1 · Board 2 · Plans 3 · Brain 4 · Worker Types 5 · Remotes 6.
- Board = the existing Kanban (Working / PR Open / CI Failed / Review / Mergeable / Done), kept as its own tab, restyled to this design.
- The Pull requests list is removed: PR state shows on each node.
- PR review and Marginalia comments live in the detail panel when a worker is selected.
